Article Title: Asian Games Medal Tally: How two kabaddi golds helped India break back into top 10 as China pull ahead
Article Text:
India won gold medals in both men's and women's kabaddi events.

Seven medals, kabaddi gold double the highlight

Anahat, Abhay keep gold hopes alive

China stretches lead at the top

Asian Games Medal Tally after Day 7

Rank Nation Gold Silver Bronze Total 1 China 107 41 28 176 2 Japan 31 49 49 129 3 South Korea 16 21 36 73 4 Uzbekistan 8 17 9 34 5 Kazakhstan 8 8 19 35 6 Thailand 8 7 9 24 7 Iran 7 14 7 28 8 Bahrain 7 2 2 11 9 North Korea 5 5 4 14 10 INDIA 4 12 14 30

NEW DELHI: India returned to the top 10 of the Asian Games medal standings on Saturday after a seven-medal haul, highlighted by two gold medals in kabaddi. The country’s gold rush in the sport, along with medals in athletics, shooting and squash, took the overall tally to 30 and moved India up to 10th place.India now have four gold, 12 silver and 14 bronze medals after seven days of competition in Aichi-Nagoya.The kabaddi teams provided the biggest boost to India’s medal count, with both the women and men successfully defending their Asian Games titles. The women defeated Iran in the final before the men followed suit later in the day, maintaining India’s remarkable dominance in the sport.India also collected medals across athletics and shooting. Sawan Barwal produced one of the standout performances of the day by winning a historic silver in the marathon, while Prachi Choudhary claimed bronze in the women’s 400m.Two-time defending champion Tajinderpal Singh Toor added another silver in the men’s shot put. Toor produced a season’s best 20.64m but could not complete a hat-trick of Asian Games gold medals after Iran’s Mohammadreza Tayebise won with a Games Record 20.81m.At the shooting range, Tilottama Sen, Vidarsa Vinod and Ashi Chouksey combined to win silver in the women’s 50m rifle 3 positions team event.India also added a bronze in squash, with Joshna Chinappa and Velavan Senthilkumar losing 1-2 to Hong Kong’s Tang Ming Hong and Lee Ka Yi in the mixed doubles semifinal.India’s squash campaign received a major boost as Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh advanced to their respective singles finals. Both remain in contention for gold as well as qualification spots for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where squash will make its debut.The men’s hockey team also progressed to the semifinals after beating Japan 2-0 in their final pool match.While India climbed back into the top 10, China continued to dominate the medal standings. The Asian giants have already crossed the 100-gold mark and lead the table with 107 gold, 41 silver and 28 bronze medals, taking their overall haul to 176.Hosts Japan remained second with 31 gold medals, followed by South Korea with 16 and Uzbekistan with eight.India’s seven-medal haul helped close out a productive Saturday and pushed the country back into the top 10, with the focus now shifting to converting more of the growing medal opportunities into gold.
Article Summary: India won gold medals in both men's and women's kabaddi events. The country's gold rush in the sport, along with medals in athletics, shooting and squash, took the overall tally to 30. India now have four gold, 12 silver and 14 bronze medals after seven days of competition in aichi-nagoya.

Article Title: Naomi Osaka heard a 9-year-old’s tennis dream in Cameroon, then made an unexpected move that could change the young player’s journey and take her closer to the biggest stage
Article Text:

Naomi Osaka backs Cameroonian tennis prodigy Uma Bogso with landmark scholarship to train at Mouratoglou Tennis Academy

Scholarship detail Information Young player Uma Bogso Age at scholarship 9 years old Country Cameroon Sport Tennis Support initiative Play Academy with Naomi Osaka Training destination Mouratoglou Academy Location Biot, near Nice, France Main opportunity Professional coaching and advanced tennis facilities

A childhood dream suddenly receives global attention

Naomi Osaka gives Uma Bogso landmark scholarship

Naomi Osaka’s Play Academy expands global mission

Naomi Osaka has had a big impact on tennis beyond her own Grand Slam career, with her Play Academy initiative to help girls access the sport. One story that stood out was that of Uma Bogso, a 9-year-old tennis player from Cameroon whose ambitions caught Osaka’s attention.The initiative did not let geography and limited resources define Uma’s opportunities, and it granted her a scholarship to train at the Mouratoglou Academy in France. The move was an opportunity for the young player to be exposed to professional coaching, high-level facilities and an international tennis environment that had previously been well beyond her regular training setup.It started with Uma idolising Naomi Osaka and dreaming of being a professional tennis player. The Cameroonian player was only 9 years old and already playing the sport with far fewer resources than many young athletes training in established tennis systems.Play Academy with Naomi Osaka provided an individual scholarship that enabled Uma to attend the Mouratoglou Academy in France. The scholarship allowed the young player to train at a state-of-the-art tennis center, work with professional coaching staff and mingle with other junior players, Play Academy said.The scholarship was important, in part, because Play Academy was established primarily to help grassroots organisations, not to regularly fund individual athletes. Therefore, Uma’s case offered a unique opportunity in the initiative and illustrated how the situation of a particular young player could be given direct attention.The opportunity also created an environment for Uma that was built around athlete development. The Mouratoglou Academy says its methodology relies on individualised coaching, listening, performance development and helping athletes progress on and off the court.Uma’s story demonstrates what a difference access can make at the very beginning of a young athlete’s development. Talent alone does not guarantee a pathway into competitive sport, especially where coaching, facilities, tournament exposure and financial resources are limited.Also, a new tennis environment can offer a 9-year-old player experiences that go beyond the improvement of individual strokes. Playing with different players can expose you to new standards of competition, new routines, and it can also show you what a longer-term pathway in tennis can look like.That wider development is in line with the philosophy of Play Academy. The initiative was launched in 2020 by Naomi Osaka, Nike and Laureus Sport for Good, with a stated aim of increasing girls’ participation in sport and supporting organisations working with girls in underserved communities.Naomi Osaka’s involvement gave Uma’s story a key connection to a player who’s felt the pressure of top-tier tennis firsthand. Osaka has four Grand Slam singles titles and has used her platform to talk about the importance of creating opportunities for girls in sport. Osaka wanted other girls to have the same opportunities and role models on their own sporting journey that she had, Play Academy said.For Uma, the scholarship was a concrete training opportunity rooted in that larger mission. Instead of just receiving encouragement, she was able to move into a professional academy environment and work with coaches who were geared to develop junior players.The Mouratoglou Academy is located in Sophia Antipolis on the French Riviera, near Nice and Cannes. Today its facilities include 33 clay and hard courts, eight indoor courts, a fitness room, sports medicine facilities, swimming pools and accommodation options for young players.The academy also says its coaching philosophy is designed to fit individual athletes, rather than to use one method. Its methodology is based on listening to players, individual coaching, development of performance and continuous assessment.So the significance of the move is not just the number of hours spent on a tennis court. A structured academy can expose a young athlete to training habits, competition preparation and routines that are hard to replicate without access to specialised facilities.Support for Uma is part of a much larger mission established through Play Academy with Naomi Osaka. Launched in Japan in 2020 with Nike and Laureus Sport for Good, the program has focused on supporting grassroots organisations using sport to create opportunities for girls.The initiative was based on a problem beyond the game of tennis. Financial, social and access barriers can make it more difficult for girls to continue to participate in sport. Play Academy has therefore adopted an approach that has included funding, capacity-building support and gender inclusive coaching and not just elite competition.Uma’s scholarship illustrated how that philosophy could intersect with an individual athlete whose circumstances were especially compelling. Going from Cameroon to a top European tennis academy was a chance to go from very little local resources to a very structured international training setting.For a player who was only 9 years old when the opportunity presented itself, the real value of it may not be in the immediate results, but in the doors it opened along the way. Naomi Osaka’s decision gave Uma’s dream a whole new context, providing a young Cameroonian tennis player with a glimpse of how far that dream could take her.
Article Summary: Naomi osaka backs cameroonian tennis prodigy uma bogso with landmark scholarship to train at mouratoglou tennis academy. The initiative did not let geography and limited resources define uma’s opportunities, and it granted her a scholarship. The move was an opportunity for the young player to be exposed to professional coaching and high-level facilities.

Article Title: Sreeshankar, Solomon reach long jump final as Tejaswin slips to third in decathlon

Nagoya: Murali Sreeshankar and David Patturaj Solomon advanced to the men's long jump final at the ongoing Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Sunday, giving India a double representation in the medal event.Sreeshankar finished second in Group B with a best effort of 7.84m. Solomon, meanwhile, secured third place in Group A after recording a best jump of 7.62m.India also had two athletes progress from the women's 400m hurdles heats, with Vithya Ramraj and Anu Raghavan both finishing second in their respective heats.Vithya clocked a season-best 55.73 seconds, while Anu produced a personal best of 55.84 seconds to book their places in the final.Tejaswin Shankar dropped from first to third in the decathlon standings after the discus throw event on Sunday.He had entered the discus as the leader after finishing third in his 110m hurdles heat in 14.33 seconds, a performance that earned him 932 points. His overall tally moved to 5,869 points, leaving him third, with athletes from China and Japan occupying the top two positions.The final two events of the decathlon, the pole vault and javelin throw, are not exactly Tejaswin's strengths.India endured a difficult day in Kurash, with several athletes making early exits.Vishal was knocked out in the men's +90kg quarterfinals after a 0-5 loss to Thailand's Kunathip Yea-On.Sangita Balhara went down 10-0 to Charmea Quelino of the Philippines in her round-of-32 bout. Article Title: Asian Games 2026: Ankush Panghal punches India’s first boxing medal with 5-0 quarterfinal win
Article Text:
Ankush Panghal auures India of maiden boxing medal at Asian Games

Ankush dominates first two rounds

Salimov fights back, but Ankush holds firm

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kurash campaign ends for Indian athletes

Reigning Commonwealth Games champion Ankush Panghal delivered a commanding performance on Sunday to assure India of its first boxing medal at the Asian Games 2026, defeating Tajikistan's Nekruz Salimov by a unanimous 5-0 decision in the men's 80kg quarterfinals.Ankush controlled the contest for most of the three rounds, using his speed, sharp combinations and solid defence to establish a decisive advantage before holding off a late challenge from Salimov.The Indian boxer came out aggressively and immediately put Salimov under pressure with a combination of right hooks and crisp 1-2 punches. Ankush won the opening round unanimously, with all five judges scoring it in his favour. He continued to dictate the pace in the second round, showcasing his movement and counter-punching ability while making it difficult for Salimov to land clean shots.His powerful left hook proved particularly effective as he secured another 5-0 verdict in the second round, leaving the Tajik boxer needing a major turnaround in the final three minutes.With his tournament on the line, Salimov came out with greater urgency in the third round and looked to land heavier punches in search of a knockdown.The Tajik boxer managed to connect with a few shots and took the final round 4-1 on the judges' scorecards. However, Ankush had already built a comfortable lead and remained composed until the final bell.Four judges scored the bout 29-28 in Ankush's favour, while the fifth judge awarded him a 30-27 victory, completing a convincing 5-0 win. The quarterfinal victory guarantees Ankush at least a bronze medal, while the CWG champion will now turn his attention to the semifinals as he bids to go one step further.India's campaign in kurash, meanwhile, suffered a series of setbacks on Sunday. Vishal was knocked out in the men's +90kg quarterfinals after losing 5-0 to Thailand's Kunathip Yea-On.In the women's -57kg category, Sangita Balhara suffered a 10-0 defeat against the Philippines' Charmea Quelino in the Round of 32. Bharti was eliminated in the Round of 16 after losing to Iran's Tahereh Azarpeivand, while Yash Kumar Chauhan also exited the men's +90kg competition following a 10-0 defeat to Tajikistan's Shakarmamad Mirmamadov.
Article Summary: Ankush panghal beats nekruz salimov 5-0 in men's 80kg quarterfinals. Win assures india of its first boxing medal at the asian games 2026. India's campaign in kurash suffered a series of setbacks on sunday.

Article Title: UFC lightweight champion Justin Gaethje admits he may never have beaten Khabib Nurmagomedov despite winning first round
Article Text:
Justin Gaethje (Image Via Getty)

Justin Gaethje says Khabib Nurmagomedov’s pressure changed the fight

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Justin Gaethje has admitted he still does not know whether he could have beaten Khabib Nurmagomedov in their UFC 254 fight. Gaethje won the opening round on two of the three judges’ scorecards. However, the UFC lightweight champion said the effort required to survive Khabib’s pressure left him with little energy for what followed.“I wasn’t gonna win that fight after the first round,” Gaethje said. He said that winning the first round had taken everything out of him. Khabib eventually took Gaethje down early in the second round and submitted him with a triangle choke at 1:34. The loss was Gaethje’s only fight against the undefeated Russian.Justin Gaethje entered UFC 254 as one of the biggest threats to Khabib Nurmagomedov’s undefeated record. The fight took place on October 24, 2020, on Fight Island in Abu Dhabi. Khabib was defending his UFC lightweight title.Gaethje started strongly. He attacked Khabib’s lead leg with powerful kicks and looked to keep the fight standing. His striking gave Nurmagomedov problems during the opening minutes.The first round was extremely demanding for both fighters.Khabib continued moving forward and applying Nurmagomedov. He also secured a takedown late in the round and moved into a dominant position.Despite that, two judges scored the round 10-9 for Gaethje. Derek Cleary gave the round to Khabib.Gaethje has now opened up on how much energy he had used during those five minutes. He said on One Night With Steiny, “I beat Khabib in the first round on two of the three scorecards, and it took everything in my body to win that first round. I wasn’t going to win after that. I think it could have been just his pressure.”The second round showed exactly what Gaethje was talking about.Gaethje opened the round with another heavy leg kick. Khabib timed it perfectly. He caught the kick and immediately closed the distance.Gaethje tapped, but referee Jason Herzog did not immediately see it. The submission continued until Gaethje lost consciousness at 1:34 of the second round.The victory moved Khabib’s professional record to 29-0. He then shocked the MMA world by announcing his retirement. Khabib removed his gloves and placed them inside the Octagon.The fight also became an important part of Khabib’s legacy. He officially lost only two rounds on judges’ scorecards during his professional career.The first came against Conor McGregor at UFC 229. McGregor won the third round on all three scorecards before Khabib finished him by submission in the fourth.The second was the opening round against Gaethje.Khabib went on to retire undefeated after UFC 254. Gaethje, meanwhile, continued competing at the top level of the lightweight division.For Gaethje, the question of whether a rematch would have produced a different result remains unanswered. He has acknowledged that the energy required to deal with Khabib in the first round made the rest of the fight extremely difficult.
Article Summary: Justin gaethje says khabib nurmagomedov’s pressure changed the fight for him. Ufc lightweight champion says winning the first round had taken everything out of him. He admits he still does not know whether he could have beaten the undefeated russian.

Article Title: Norma Dumont makes her bout personal with NSFW move at Ailin Perez in wild UFC Vegas 121 faceoff
Article Text:
Norma Dumont vs Ailin Perez. Image via: UFC

Norma Dumont tosses co**oms and cash at Ailin Perez in unexpected UFC scene

Norma Dumont vs Ailin Perez : Fight details, date and time

Norma Dumont had little interest in keeping Friday’s UFC Vegas 121 faceoff routine.The Brazilian brought co**oms to the stage before her staredown with Ailin Perez, and the strange prop soon became the focus of the confrontation. Perez performed her trademark twerking celebration during the faceoff, prompting Dumont to pull the co**oms from her shorts and throw them toward her rival.“You need this,” Dumont said with a smile.Perez then picked up the items, but Dumont was not finished. She followed by tossing a wad of cash toward the Argentine fighter, adding another pointed message to an exchange that had already become uncomfortable.“You pay ***** with money. Take it, it’s yours,” Dumont said.The moment was only one part of a tense faceoff. Perez jumped off the stage to collect the items, and UFC officials eventually had to step in after the fighters exchanged words and appeared close to another physical confrontation.Previously, Perez made a huge claim that Dumont’s boyfriend, Marco Tulio, had been watching her while she trained. Dumont rejected the suggestion, saying Perez had repeatedly tagged Tulio in social media posts.The dispute added a personal layer to a matchup that already carried plenty of competitive tension.Perez has also described earlier friction between the two fighters, including an alleged confrontation at the UFC Performance Institute. Her account of that incident has not been confirmed by Dumont, giving the rivalry another point of disagreement heading into fight night.Dumont, meanwhile, has made it clear she wants to settle the issue inside the Octagon. The Brazilian said she now has a sanctioned opportunity to handle her differences with Perez through the fight rather than outside it.Norma Dumont and Ailin Perez are scheduled to meet Saturday, September 26, at the Meta APEX in Las Vegas. Their women’s bantamweight contest is the co-main event of UFC Vegas 121, beneath the Raul Rosas Jr. vs. Raoni Barcelos matchup.Dumont enters the fight with a 13-3 record, while Perez is 13-2. The Brazilian was listed second and the Argentine fifth in the UFC women’s bantamweight rankings as of June, according to the supplied fight-week report. Perez also owns a six-fight active UFC winning streak. Dumont is looking to respond after her six-fight run ended with a unanimous-decision loss to Joselyne Edwards in April.The fight is scheduled to air live from Las Vegas, with UFC's official social post listing an 8 p.m. ET start on Paramount+.The unusual weigh-in exchange has added another chapter to a rivalry that already had plenty of history. Once the cage door closes, though, the talking will give way to the fight itself.

Indian athlete Baranica Elangovan won the bronze medal in the women's pole vault at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, on Friday, giving India its first-ever medal in the event at the Asian Games.The 29-year-old secured the bronze with a best clearance of 4.15m. She shared the medal with Kazakhstan's Polina Ivanova, who also cleared 4.15m. The two athletes matched each other on countback, resulting in a shared bronze.Baranica began with first-attempt clearances of 3.85m and 4.00m before needing two attempts to clear 4.15m. She then attempted 4.25m but failed on all three attempts, ending her competition with the bronze medal.Her compatriot Sindhushree Ganesha exited the competition without registering a mark, while Baranica remained in contention for a medal.Baranica has also had a strong season, improving the national record twice earlier this year. She first cleared 4.22m in March and then raised the mark to 4.23m in May at Bhubaneswar. Sindhushree G later improved the national record to 4.25m in June. Baranica's season-best remains 4.23m.The pole vaulter from Tamil Nadu had suffered an ACL injury in 2020 and went through a challenging period of rehabilitation, after which she moved to the Reliance Foundation High Performance Centre in Bhubaneswar in 2023.Japan's Misaki Morota won the gold with a best clearance of 4.55m, while China's Chunge Neu took silver with 4.50m.Baranica's bronze took India's overall medal tally at the Asian Games to 23, including two gold, nine silver and 12 bronze medals.

Article Title: Chess Olympiad Round 9: D Gukesh channels his world champion self, overturns almost-lost game to keep India in gold hunt
Article Text:
Dommaraju Gukesh of India (Photo by Rafal Oleksiewicz for FIDE)

How Gukesh turned the tables on Donchenko

Vantika, Divya lead India's women to victory

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Since becoming world champion two years ago, noise has followed Dommaraju Gukesh almost everywhere, at times making it feel as though he isn't worthy of the title he rightfully won.But on Friday, when India needed the youngest world champion in history to deliver a win, he did exactly that, turning around an almost-lost position to beat Germany's Alexander Donchenko in Round 9 of the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.It was the kind of performance that felt like it could quiet the criticism all on its own.Playing black, Gukesh traded off his dark-squared bishop early to damage White's pawn structure, then spent the middlegame manoeuvring patiently, repositioning knights, expanding on the queenside with a5-a4, and probing for weaknesses without rushing.For a long stretch, the position stayed murky and roughly balanced, with both sides shuffling pieces and neither able to land a clean blow.It was in the run-up to the time control that things turned dangerous for Gukesh. Donchenko doubled his rooks on the e-file and pushed one all the way to e6, aiming squarely at Black's king, which had been forced to step out to f7 for safety.With his own clock running low, Gukesh had to defend precisely while trying to generate counterplay of his own on the kingside, pushing his h- and g-pawns forward to create complications.It was a position where one careless move could have ended the game in White's favour.Gukesh held his nerve. As the pawn storms and piece trades settled down, he found a route to activate his queen and knight while White's pieces drifted out of coordination.The Chennai-born grandmaster found an excellent move with 51...Nf4. The German sacked Gukesh's knight with 52.Rxf4, but Donchenko's bishop was thus left hanging on c3; Gukesh's queen swooped in to capture it, and from there it was a matter of technique.A check with his queen forced Donchenko's king into an impossible spot, and White resigned rather than play on a piece down with his king exposed.Elsewhere on the board, Nihal Sarin, playing white, spent much of his game in some turmoil against Frederik Svane but held firm for a draw.With Gukesh's win already banked, Praggnanandhaa and Arjun Erigaisi didn't need to force matters either, settling for draws against Vincent Keymer and Matthias Bluebaum, respectively. India closed out the match 2.5-1.5.With the win, India moved to 15 points, still one point behind hosts Uzbekistan, who beat the United States on Friday to stay in front.India's women's team also had a productive Friday, with Vantika Agrawal and Divya Deshmukh both delivering important wins to seal the match against Uzbekistan.Vantika, playing white against Nilufarkhon Imomkuzieva, picked up an early pawn with a sharp tactical sequence; a check with her queen forced Black's king to give up material before the middlegame had properly begun.She nursed that small material edge through a long, technical battle, trading down into a rook endgame where her extra pawn and more active king proved decisive.Pushing her kingside pawns forward in the closing stages, Vantika eventually broke through, and Imomkuzieva had no way to hold the position together.Divya Deshmukh's game against Gulrukhbegim Tokhirjonova was a far longer and more chaotic affair.Both sides grabbed material early. Tokhirjonova's knight snatched a pawn on b7 just as Divya's queen picked up a stray piece on d2, leaving the position roughly balanced but sharp.What followed was a marathon battle through the middlegame and into a complex rook, knight and bishop endgame, with both players navigating tricky technical positions deep into the game.Divya's technique held up better over the long haul, and after 73 hard-fought moves, Tokhirjonova had nothing left to stop Black's advancing king, resigning the position.Those two results were enough to see India through the match, keeping the team firmly in the mix for a medal.As things stand, India's women sit second in the standings on 15 points, behind an in-form Chinese side on 17.With two rounds left, India's hopes of gold now depend largely on whether China slip up, but on Friday's evidence, neither Indian team looks inclined to make things easy for anyone chasing them either.In the Open section, India face Uzbekistan 2, while the women’s team take on China in the penultimate round of the Chess Olympiad.
Article Summary: Dommaraju gukesh beats germany's alexander donchenko in round 9 of the 46th chess olympiad in samarkand, uzbekistan. India's women's team also had a productive friday, with vantika agrawal and divya deshmukh both delivering important wins to seal the match. Tokhirjonova's knight snatched a pawn on b7 just as divya's queen picked up a stray piece on d2.

Article Title: Asian Games: Abhay Singh wins silver after spirited fight in men's squash final

NEW DELHI: India’s Abhay Singh claimed the silver medal in the men’s singles squash event at the Asian Games 2026, going down 0–3 to Malaysia’s Ng Eain Yow in the gold-medal match on Sunday. The Indian stayed competitive in the opening game before the world No. 17 took control, winning 11–9, 11–5, 11–5 to secure the title.World No. 26 Abhay, who had advanced to the final without major difficulty, was bidding to add another chapter to India’s strong history in men’s singles squash at the continental showpiece. But Ng’s consistency and ability to respond to the Indian’s attacking play proved decisive.The silver gives India another medal in squash, with attention now turning to the women’s singles final, where Anahat Singh is set to face Malaysia’s Sivasangari Subramaniam.The final began with both players trading points, as Abhay looked to put pressure on Ng with his attacking shots. The Malaysian held a narrow 4–3 advantage in the early exchanges, but the Indian stayed close and continued to find ways to challenge his opponent.Abhay produced one of the standout moments of the opening game with a clever change of angle at the last moment. With Ng anticipating the shot to go in another direction, Abhay’s adjustment caught the Malaysian off guard and kept the Indian within reach at 8–7.Ng, however, managed the closing stages better to take the first game 11–9. The narrow margin left Abhay with reason to believe he could turn the contest around, but the Malaysian carried the momentum into the second.Ng raised his level in the second game, taking it 11–5 to move within one game of the gold medal. Abhay faced the challenge of winning three consecutive games to overturn the deficit, but the Malaysian continued to dictate the rallies and limit the Indian’s opportunities.Abhay made a bright start to the third game, moving 4–2 ahead and briefly suggesting a possible fightback. Ng responded quickly, though, and gradually reclaimed the lead. The Malaysian moved ahead 6–5, with Abhay still within a point, but Ng’s steady play helped him close out the game 11–5 and complete the straight-games victory.The result brought Abhay’s run to a close with a silver medal, while Ng added the Asian Games men’s singles title to his campaign.

Article Title: Two sold-out Ed Sheeran concerts at Massachusetts’ Gillette Stadium were canceled hours before the weekend shows; the venue cited severe nor’easter warnings, with fans promised refunds as the storm th
Article Text: Ed Sheeran’s two sold-out concerts at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, were canceled just hours before the scheduled performances as a powerful nor’easter threatened New England. The cancellation was reported by the BBC, CBS Boston and Boston 25 News, with the venue and tour promoter pointing to severe weather conditions and safety concerns. The shows, scheduled for Friday, September 25, and Saturday, September 26, were part of Sheeran’s ongoing Loop Tour. Both dates were listed as canceled on Ticketmaster, with the concerts originally scheduled to begin at 8 p.m.The decision came as a major fall nor’easter moved toward the region, bringing the threat of heavy rain, strong winds, coastal flooding and rough surf across parts of New England. Local weather warnings remained in effect through the weekend, prompting concerns about travel as well as conditions at the outdoor stadium.Gillette Stadium said the decision followed consultations with local officials, the promoter and the tour. The venue said safety was the priority and confirmed that refunds would be available through the original point of purchase. Fans who bought their tickets through Ticketmaster were set to receive automatic refunds.The abrupt cancellation marked another disruption for Sheeran’s US tour, which has already faced significant attention in recent weeks over the removal of rapper Macklemore as an opening act.Macklemore had performed on earlier dates of the tour while making outspoken comments supporting Palestinians and calling for a ceasefire in Gaza. Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots and operator of Gillette Stadium, had objected to Macklemore’s appearances following those comments. The rapper was subsequently removed from the remaining tour dates, with the promoter saying venue owners would not allow him to perform. Sheeran has said the decision was made by his promoter rather than by him.The controversy also prompted several artists connected with the tour to withdraw. Sheeran returned to the stage in Philadelphia on September 19 with a new backing lineup and addressed the turmoil surrounding the tour. The Massachusetts shows were therefore already among the most closely watched dates on the Loop Tour. Their cancellation, however, was officially attributed to the weather rather than the earlier dispute.For ticket holders, the immediate concern was whether they would be able to recover the money spent on the canceled performances. The stadium confirmed that refunds were available, while Ticketmaster’s event listings now show both September 25 and September 26 performances as canceled.Sheeran’s next listed US performances are scheduled to continue in October, with dates at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta on October 3 and Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis on October 10.
Article Summary: Ed sheeran’s two sold-out concerts at gillette stadium in foxborough, massachusetts, were canceled just hours before the scheduled performances. The cancellation was reported by the bbc, cbs boston and boston 25 news, with the venue and tour promoter pointing to severe weather conditions and safety concerns.

Article Title: Nike Alphafly 4 launched with lighter ZoomX LT foam and 10% more energy return
Article Text:
Nike Alphafly 4 are 5% lighter than Alphafly 3

Two foams now sandwich the plate

The upper is designed for tired feet

Nike has launched the Alphafly 4, the newest version of its marathon racing shoe, with changes to nearly every major part. The company says it returns 10% more energy than its predecessor and weighs 5% less in a men's size 8.5.The biggest change is in the midsole. Nike has added a new ZoomX LT foam, which it says is up to 17% lighter than standard ZoomX and offers 8% more energy return. The shoe goes on early, limited sale on nike.com from today, September 17, with wider availability on nike.com and at select stores from October 29.ZoomX LT doesn't fully replace regular ZoomX. Nike layers the two foams above and below the carbon-fibre Flyplate, which keeps the Alphafly's signature propulsive scoop. The plate adds stability and guides a smooth forward roll, which should help runners hold a steady cadence. Up front, dual Air Zoom units have been retuned to work alongside the foam and plate at push-off. A lightweight Fast Shot outsole handles grip.The new Atomknit upper is seamless and breathable. It uses zoned midfoot cables, an integrated heel unit and a molded sock liner to hold the foot securely over long distances.Nike says development drew on athlete feedback across Alphafly generations, learnings from Project Dreamweaver, and extensive women's trials. Emily Farina, Senior Principal, Running Footwear, Nike Sport Research Lab, said the team studied how fatigue changes running mechanics."Our goal was simple: create a shoe that helps athletes feel more confident and capable deep into the race," she said.Nike athlete Addisu Gobena has already tested that claim. He wore the Alphafly 4 to a course-record marathon win in Sydney, and said he trusted the shoe when the race got difficult.
Article Summary: Nike alphafly 4 is the newest version of its marathon racing shoe. The company says it returns 10% more energy than its predecessor and weighs 5% less in a men's size 8.5. Nike has added a new zoomx lt foam, which it says is up to 17% lighter than standard zoomx.

Article Title: Asian Games 2026: What Indian medallists can earn in cash rewards, government jobs and state incentives
Article Text:

How much does an individual medallist receive?

Team medals: the calculation changes

Multiple medals and the highest-award rule

Can Asian Games medallists get government jobs?

State incentives can add another layer

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India’s medal winners at the Asian Games 2026 could return home with more than a place on the podium. Along with national recognition, athletes who win gold, silver or bronze are eligible for cash awards under a central government scheme. They may also qualify for sports-quota jobs and additional incentives announced by their respective state governments.The central cash awards are laid out in the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports’ “Special Awards to Medal Winners in International Sports Events and their Coaches” scheme. The scheme, first introduced in 1986, has been revised over time, with the stated aim of rewarding sporting achievement, encouraging higher performance and inspiring young people to take up sports.For an individual Asian Games medal, the listed central award is Rs 30 lakh for gold, Rs 20 lakh for silver and Rs 10 lakh for bronze. These are the base figures: the amount for a team medal depends on the size of the team and the scheme’s rules for calculating and distributing awards.Under the central scheme, Asian Games and Commonwealth Games medal awards are the same. Olympic medal awards are higher.The same corresponding award amounts apply to Para Games medal winners.The cash incentive is subject to the eligibility criteria and conditions prescribed by the government.That means an Indian athlete who wins an individual gold in Aichi-Nagoya could be eligible for a central award of Rs 30 lakh. A silver medallist’s listed award is Rs 20 lakh, while a bronze medallist’s is Rs 10 lakh.For team events, the scheme determines the award using the number of athletes in the team on the ground. The multiplier is applied to the corresponding individual-event award for the competition, medal and category.A team of two receives 1.5 times the corresponding award; a team of three or four receives twice the award; a team of five to 10 receives three times the award; and a team with more than 10 members receives five times the award. The resulting amount is shared equally among the team members, with a condition that no member receives less than 50% of the corresponding individual-event award.The scheme defines team events as competitions in which athletes compete collectively, and says incentives are awarded to all team members, including bench or reserve players, in accordance with the international standards applicable to each sport. It also provides that, in specified sports disciplines, each team member’s cash incentive is 75% of the incentive amount applicable to the corresponding individual event, based on the medal, level and participation category.These provisions mean that a team medal cannot simply be treated as the same flat award for every athlete. The final amount depends on the event’s classification, team strength and applicable scheme provisions.The scheme also addresses athletes who win more than one medal at an international event. As a general rule, a sportsperson who wins multiple medals in individual or team categories is eligible for the cash incentive only for the highest-ranking medal won at that event.There is an important exception for the Olympic Games, Paralympic Games, Asian Games and Para-Asian Games: athletes who win multiple medals in individual or team categories may be eligible for the cash incentive for each medal, subject to the scheme’s terms and conditions.For an Asian Games athlete who wins more than one medal, therefore, the central award may be calculated medal by medal rather than being limited to the single highest finish. The precise amount still depends on whether the medals were won individually or as part of a team, and on the applicable team-event rules.The figures and provisions above are from the Department of Sports, Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports circular dated January 31, 2025, as provided in the scheme details.Cash awards are only one part of the potential support available to medal winners. Athletes who have represented India in recognised international competitions, including the Asian Games, may also be considered for recruitment under sports-quota provisions.At the central level, recruitment of meritorious sportspersons is governed by Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) instructions and related office memorandums. The central framework generally provides for appointment to Group C and erstwhile Group D posts, subject to eligibility, recruitment rules and the specific terms in force. It does not establish a general entitlement for every medal winner to receive a Group A or Group B post.A medal does not, by itself, mean that a job is automatically granted. Athletes must meet the relevant conditions, and appointments depend on the applicable recruitment process and rules. Serving government employees may also be covered by separate provisions, including certain out-of-turn promotion or incentive arrangements, where permitted.The amount an athlete may receive after the Games can vary further because state governments frame their own sports policies and service rules. Some states offer additional cash awards, employment opportunities or other incentives to athletes from their state who win medals at major international competitions.As a result, two Indian athletes who win the same medal at the Asian Games may be eligible for different overall benefits depending on their state’s policy and their individual circumstances. State incentives are not uniform across India, and any announced reward or job offer must be checked against the specific state’s policy, eligibility conditions and formal government orders.For athletes and families assessing what a medal could mean financially, the key distinction is between the central scheme’s published cash award and any separate state-level benefit. The central award schedule gives a clear starting point – Rs 30 lakh, Rs 20 lakh and Rs 10 lakh for individual Asian Games gold, silver and bronze – but the final package may depend on team-event calculations, multiple-medal provisions, state rules and eligibility for recruitment or other incentives.
Article Summary: India's medal winners at the asian games 2026 could return home with more than a place on the podium. Along with national recognition, athletes who win gold, silver or bronze are eligible for cash awards. They may also qualify for sports-quota jobs and additional incentives announced by their respective state governments.

Article Title: Asian Games 2026: India’s 44-year wait ends as Sawan Barwal wins silver in men’s marathon
Article Text:
India's Sawan Barwal reacts after his second place finish in the men's marathon at the Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan, Saturday, Sept. 26, 2026. (AP Photo/Lee Jin-man)

Historic medal for Indian athletics

Sawan Barwal scripted history at the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya on Saturday, winning silver in the men’s marathon and ending India’s 44-year wait for a medal in the event. He clocked a personal best of 2:11:37, finishing 48 seconds behind Japan’s Ichitaka Yamashita, who won gold in 2:10:49. China’s Peiyou Feng took bronze with 2:12:13.The marathon started at 4 a.m. IST with 19 runners, including Barwal and fellow Indian Kartik Karkera. Barwal quickly established himself among the leaders and was in second place at the halfway mark with a timing of 1:05:54. He continued to hold his position as the race entered its final stages, reaching the 35-kilometre mark in second.With around seven kilometres left, Barwal was still chasing Yamashita. The Japanese runner eventually opened up a gap, but Barwal maintained his pace and stayed firmly in silver-medal position. He finished with a timing of 2:11:37, securing India’s first Asian Games marathon medal since the 1982 Delhi Games and the country’s first medal in the event on foreign soil.The silver adds to Barwal’s growing record. In April, he broke Shivnath Singh’s 48-year-old national marathon record at the NN Marathon Rotterdam.His latest performance now converts that record-setting form into a major international medal.Barwal’s silver is India’s fourth Asian Games marathon medal. Chhota Singh won gold and Surat Singh Mathur took bronze at the inaugural 1951 Games, while Hosur Kukkappa Seetharan won another bronze in 1982.The other Indian runner, Kartik Karkera, finished 17th among 19 competitors with a time of 2:22:41.
